description: Phase 1 graph-native force/goal arbitration over language-neutral communication_evidence.v1. The language adapter supplies evidence categories; these rules derive communicative force and cognitive goal without treating grammatical kind, word order, or lexical form as the force. This is a deliberately small evidence policy, not a surface acknowledgement policy.

rules.name: arbitrate_typed_future_action_as_defer
rules.comment: A typed temporal condition changes action timing: retain it as deferred, rather than minting an active action commitment.

rules.name: arbitrate_continuing_action_as_act
rules.comment: A typed action-request interpretation in a continuation can retain its action commitment when no future condition or unresolved referent blocks it. The semantic force, not grammatical clause form, owns the action classification.

rules.name: arbitrate_partially_grounded_action_as_act
rules.comment: Partial grounding may authorize a staged action commitment when no typed temporal or unresolved dependency controls it.

rules.name: arbitrate_unbacked_proposition_confirmation_as_repair
rules.comment: A typed proposition-confirmation request is not an encyclopedia lookup. Until a conversationally grounded answer is available, ask for grounding rather than treating a lexical search result as confirmation.

rules.name: support_anaphoric_polar_relation_from_accepted_proposition
rules.comment: A discourse-grounded anaphor can answer a polar relation only when the event-bound answer topic joins an accepted, explicitly evidenced structured proposition on the same predicate and role-labelled arguments. This creates positive relation support before the missing-support repair rule runs.

rules.name: support_named_polar_relation_from_accepted_unary_proposition
rules.comment: A named-subject polar query can be answered only from an accepted, explicitly evidenced unary proposition whose predicate and subject match the selected parse and same-event answer goal. This does not treat a topic answer or a multi-argument proposition as relation support.

rules.name: select_affirmative_polar_answer_from_accepted_proposition
rules.comment: Native cognition selects yes only when an accepted, explicitly evidenced proposition matches the queried relation and its polarity matches the neutral question-polarity evidence. The plan is semantic; the language faculty realizes its affirmative value.

rules.name: select_negative_polar_answer_from_accepted_proposition
rules.comment: Native cognition selects no only when an accepted, explicitly evidenced proposition matches the queried relation and its polarity differs from the neutral question-polarity evidence. The plan is semantic; the language faculty realizes its negative value.

rules.name: arbitrate_unbacked_topic_polar_relation_as_repair
rules.comment: Topic grounding is not support for a polar relation. When a same-event topic-answer goal has no matching supported proposition, preserve the information request and repair rather than release a topic sentence as a relation answer. Capability and reflective questions without an answer_topic goal remain with their own faculties.

rules.name: arbitrate_topic_candidate_without_polar_relation_support_as_repair
rules.comment: A topic answer candidate that matches a polar request cannot substitute for proposition-level support of the queried relation.

rules.name: clear_lexical_concept_grounding_without_polar_relation_support
rules.comment: An exact lexical Concept may identify the topic word but does not ground an unsupported polar proposition. Clear only that lexical-only path after native repair selection; preserve independently supported discourse, HeldAnswer, and proposition evidence paths.

rules.name: arbitrate_compound_social_polar_question_without_support_as_repair
rules.comment: A compound greeting-plus-polar-question preserves both act records while the unsupported question component selects clarification. This narrowly scoped rule does not assert a readiness answer or erase the social co-act.

rules.name: arbitrate_complete_turn_action_request_as_act
rules.comment: A complete language-neutral imperative action request may select act only on a turn-compatible event and only when it is not a correction, social coordination, or typed unresolved action reference. Non-turn actions and partial events retain their separate defer/repair rules.

rules.name: arbitrate_standalone_grounded_action_request_as_act
rules.comment: A standalone event is still an event-bound directive when language-neutral action force, the graph-transported instruction parse, a resolved reference, and grounded action evidence all agree. Grammatical literal-form labels are not required to agree with the selected semantic parse. This selects an action goal only; the separate instruction/world capability gate must still establish whether anything can be performed. Future-conditioned, unresolved, social, correction, and unsupported-world cases remain excluded.

rules.name: arbitrate_missing_world_information_request_as_blocked
rules.comment: Unavailable world evidence blocks fulfillment without erasing the language-neutral information-request force or its linked goal.

rules.name: arbitrate_missing_world_support_as_blocked
rules.comment: A language adapter's explicit missing-world-support evidence is a blocked state, not a clarification repair or an action commitment.

rules.name: arbitrate_turn_compatible_request_without_authority_as_blocked
rules.comment: A complete response-slot information request whose typed action frame lacks authority must receive a native blocked disposition; referent grounding alone cannot authorize the requested recommendation or action.

rules.name: arbitrate_unresolved_anaphoric_reason_request_as_repair
rules.comment: A typed causal question with missing causal support remains a repair when its graph-bound topic is an unresolved anaphor; do not substitute a lexical answer about the pronoun candidate.

rules.name: arbitrate_reason_request_without_causal_support_as_learning
rules.comment: A well-formed typed reason request whose topic is known but causal path is absent selects learning/retrieval, not user repair. Missing answer evidence is not evidence that the user's request needs repair.

rules.name: arbitrate_unresolved_compound_action_as_action_repair
rules.comment: A compound event can preserve its action-request goal while native cognition repairs an unresolved member; the repair disposition prevents partial release, while act_or_clarify retains the selected communicative intent.

rules.name: arbitrate_typed_unresolved_action_dependency_as_repair
rules.comment: Native cognition selects repair when an imperative has a typed unresolved graph/reference dependency. The parse dependency is sufficient evidence; corpus uncertainty annotations are not runtime inputs.

rules.name: arbitrate_unresolved_imperative_information_request_as_repair
rules.comment: Some imperative constructions are typed as information requests while still carrying an unresolved referent dependency. Preserve the information-request force, but select native repair from the explicit unresolved parse evidence.

rules.name: defer_unresolved_nonturn_response_action_request
rules.comment: An unresolved action request in a non-turn response slot cannot authorize acting on an implicit antecedent. Preserve it as deferred until graph-grounded action context is available; route or reply heuristics cannot create that authority.

rules.name: arbitrate_typed_continuation_fragment_as_defer
rules.comment: A typed non-turn continuation fragment defers the incomplete event instead of emitting a turn-level repair pair; parser-derived fragment status and stream relation are sufficient evidence.

rules.name: arbitrate_nonturn_knowledge_deficit_continuation_as_repair
rules.comment: A typed knowledge-deficit continuation selects repair cognition even when the non-turn boundary has no response slot; keep disposition selection native and release separately guarded.

rules.name: arbitrate_addressed_attention_request_as_social_act
rules.comment: A language adapter's typed polite vocative-attention construction is social coordination, not a world-action commitment; native cognition records the social disposition.

rules.name: arbitrate_corrective_discourse_response_as_defer
rules.comment: A typed corrective discourse relation in a response uses its action clause to update common ground rather than execute a world action.

rules.name: arbitrate_declarative_correction_as_defer
rules.comment: A language-adapter-typed declarative correction in a response updates common ground without requiring an imperative parse or claiming the correction itself was executed.

rules.name: index_grounded_instruction_target_in_discourse_event
rules.comment: Native index of a grounded instruction's typed action-target interpretation on its discourse event. Later scoped rules consume this event-local edge instead of joining every event in the discourse history.

rules.name: carry_scoped_action_target_across_topicless_event
rules.comment: Carry an indexed grounded action target across a topicless discourse event only when event order and speaker/addressee direction remain continuous. A new topic or action does not inherit the old target.

rules.name: ground_definite_correction_from_scoped_action_target
rules.comment: Native reference grounding: a typed definite subject in a correction is linked only to an earlier grounded instruction target carried on the immediately preceding discourse event with the same parser-provided head and speaker/addressee direction. The rule grounds the referent, not the truth of the corrected proposition.
effects: CommunicationInterpretation -> discourse-scoped DiscourseState -> prior grounded DiscourseEvent -> matching action-target head

rules.name: arbitrate_nonturn_action_as_defer
rules.comment: A standalone, sufficiently grounded non-turn action may be retained as a deferred commitment. Continuations and typed future conditions have their own rules.

rules.name: arbitrate_uncertain_continuing_common_ground_event_as_repair
rules.comment: A non-turn continuation carrying adapter-typed uncertainty about common-ground content requires repair before committing an update; native cognition does not infer correction from surface wording.

rules.name: arbitrate_explicit_failure_as_error
rules.comment: An adapter-supplied explicit failure is distinct from ordinary uncertainty. Native cognition records an error disposition before any repair surface can be released; ordinary uncertainty remains eligible for repair or defer.

rules.name: retain_typed_action_force_after_native_disposition
rules.comment: A specific native rule may settle an action request as defer/repair/blocked/etc. Preserve its arbitration basis and selected goal while filling only the still-missing force readback from the original neutral evidence.

rules.name: defer_standalone_nonturn_common_ground_update
rules.comment: A standalone, adapter-typed assertion/correction event outside a live turn may update modeled common ground, but it does not claim an interlocutor response. Generic declarative force alone is insufficient; the language adapter must supply the neutral statement_act category.

rules.name: defer_response_assertion_without_proposition_uptake
rules.comment: A parsed assertion in response position records a native defer disposition without endorsing or adopting its proposition.

rules.name: defer_continuation_assertion_without_proposition_uptake
rules.comment: A typed assertion carried as a stream continuation is recorded without treating it as an answer or endorsing its proposition. The graph-resident relation and adapter-typed assertion are sufficient; no surface-specific rule is used.

rules.name: arbitrate_event_selection_from_rule_firing_history
rules.comment: A turn-bounded RuleFiringHistory ledger is prior-event evidence. For a language-neutral event-specific selection with no event binding, native cognition selects its last progressing rule and records support; the language/reply layer may render only this selected graph evidence.

rules.name: arbitrate_unresolved_event_selection_without_history_as_repair
rules.comment: A language-neutral event-specific selection whose temporal binding is unresolved receives repair when no prior-event history supports the requested target. This rule does not depend on a text dispatch path or claim an event-history source exists.

rules.name: arbitrate_acknowledgement_as_common_ground_update
rules.comment: The language adapter may supply a typed acknowledgement distinct from a greeting/social action. Native cognition records common-ground update and defers the floor; no surface wording is inspected here.

rules.name: arbitrate_inability_response_as_error
rules.comment: A semantically typed inability to perform an action in a response position is an explicit failed-action outcome. The rule reads a neutral act kind and graph discourse relation, not lexical negation or language-specific word order.

rules.name: arbitrate_standalone_inability_as_blocked
rules.comment: A semantically typed inability to perform an action in a standalone event is blocked rather than a turn-level defer. The rule consumes neutral semantic and discourse evidence only.

rules.name: arbitrate_typed_refusal_as_defer
rules.comment: An explicit language-adapter refusal updates common ground and defers the floor. The rule consumes a neutral force category only; it does not inspect a negation token or select a surface reply.

rules.name: block_unavailable_action_in_response
rules.comment: A graph-typed action with an explicitly negated availability state in a response slot is blocked. The adapter supplies a neutral availability value; native arbitration combines it with the discourse relation without inspecting a surface pattern.

rules.name: arbitrate_typed_nonunderstanding_report_as_repair
rules.comment: A neutral adapter report of failed first-person understanding selects clarification/repair. The language adapter supplies the typed act; native cognition owns its disposition and route.

rules.name: defer_incomplete_ability_offer_without_target
rules.comment: A typed ability offer with no action target is a social act but not an acceptance candidate. A non-turn offer remains deferred; it is not converted into a generic social answer.

rules.name: repair_unresolved_ability_offer_target
rules.comment: Recognize a first-person ability offer while keeping an unresolved target in repair; target uncertainty cannot authorize acceptance or execution.

rules.name: arbitrate_typed_ability_action_offer_as_social_answer
rules.comment: A complete language-adapter offer whose selected target has a graph Concept licenses an acceptance adjacency. This proves lexical target availability only, not an instance or action capability; the reply does not authorize execution or infer success.

rules.name: arbitrate_complete_social_act_as_answer
rules.comment: A complete, typed social act is a live coordination turn. Partial fragments retain the dedicated defer policy; no surface-word recognition is used here.

rules.name: arbitrate_standalone_farewell_as_social_answer
rules.comment: A language adapter's typed farewell act licenses a social adjacency even when delivered outside a live turn. The rule consumes the neutral act category, not departure wording or a corpus label.

rules.name: arbitrate_typed_overlap_fragment_as_defer
rules.comment: Native cognition consumes an explicitly typed partial overlap event. The disposition is not inferred from a reply or from turn-taking.

rules.name: settle_unresolved_action_repair_basis
rules.comment: After generic force arbitration settles language-neutral force, retain the specific rationale whenever the adapter recorded an unresolved action referent; a corpus uncertainty label is not required.

rules.name: settle_uncertain_continuation_repair_basis
rules.comment: Retain the native uncertainty rationale after generic force arbitration has recorded assertion-or-correction force.

rules.name: arbitrate_exhausted_standalone_topic_request_as_repair
rules.comment: After the same-event standalone answer_topic attempt fails to produce verified support, a request transitions from answer/learning to repair so the interlocutor can supply or clarify the missing topic. This is a post-retrieval native transition; it cannot pre-empt supported answers, pending retrieval, permission blocks, or non-standalone discourse.

rules.name: arbitrate_unresolved_nonturn_information_request_as_repair
rules.comment: An unresolved non-turn information request selects repair when the adapter records explicit uncertainty or an unresolved reference/anaphor; a generic unknown topic remains eligible for answer/learning.

rules.name: arbitrate_unresolved_continuing_information_referent_as_repair
rules.comment: An information request in a continuing event with adapter-typed unresolved referent evidence repairs the missing discourse/world link; complete scene-description requests without that unresolved relation remain eligible for their selected faculty.

rules.name: arbitrate_uncertain_turn_information_referent_as_repair
rules.comment: In a turn-compatible information request, explicit uncertainty plus adapter-typed unresolved referent evidence requires repair. This does not consume corpus labels because the runtime evaluation boundary excludes those labels.

rules.name: arbitrate_unresolved_nonturn_frontier_as_repair
rules.comment: A non-turn standalone unresolved communication frontier requires repair. The adapter's typed frontier and unresolved grounding are sufficient; annotation-only uncertainty labels are not runtime evidence. Continuation/overlap fragments are handled by their own defer rules.

rules.name: arbitrate_uncertain_repair_response_as_repair
rules.comment: A non-turn response that explicitly reports unresolved common-ground understanding is a repair state, not a generic common-ground assertion.

rules.name: arbitrate_supported_event_topic_answer
rules.comment: A graph-selected answer_topic for this exact message, backed by a supported HeldAnswer and TopicGroundingEvidence, resolves a prior reflexive frontier hypothesis as an information answer. A goal or reply surface alone is insufficient; the native graph evidence chain is required.

rules.name: arbitrate_supported_selected_concept_answer
rules.comment: A selected concept on this exact information-request event may be answered only when a matching held answer and explicit topic-grounding evidence are graph-linked. This covers the ordinary selected-concept route without relying on reply text or surface wording.

rules.name: arbitrate_supported_event_bound_topic_goal_answer
rules.comment: A route-selected answer_topic Goal is sufficient to identify the event's topic only when it is linked to that exact message and the same topic has a supported held answer plus explicit topic-grounding evidence. This covers parse paths that preserve comp_topic rather than the legacy comp_know_concept field; it does not infer answer authority from a receipt or reply surface.

rules.name: arbitrate_unresolved_nonturn_permission_as_blocked
rules.comment: A non-turn standalone information request whose native permission check reports missing authority is blocked; do not confuse request repair with missing authorization.

rules.name: arbitrate_turn_compatible_unknown_information_request_as_learning
rules.comment: A complete response-compatible information request whose world grounding is unknown, whose reference is not anaphoric, and whose event predicate resolves to a held Concept is a learning request, not an unresolved non-turn repair. Predicate resolution is a structural guard against treating a social readiness question as external learning. This selects retrieval/learning intent only; it does not authorize an answer without graph-supported evidence.

rules.name: arbitrate_unresolved_turn_compatible_information_request_as_repair
rules.comment: A complete response-compatible information request with unresolved grounding and no selected disposition remains a native repair. A graph-linked predicate may have already selected a learning request; this fallback never grants answer authority.

rules.name: arbitrate_uncertain_selected_response_as_learning_request
rules.comment: A graph-typed uncertainty report with a selected information gap in a response slot creates a source-constrained learning request. It requests retrieval only; it does not treat the reported uncertainty or a reply surface as an answer.

rules.name: arbitrate_supported_self_organisation_answer
rules.comment: A language adapter may transport the selected reflective faculty and its graph-backed Microtheory evidence. Native arbitration alone selects answer disposition and the same-event answer Message; adapter prose is not authority.

effects.name: answer
effects.description: answers a graph-supported reflective faculty question

rules.name: arbitrate_supported_self_model_rule_answer
rules.comment: An exact self-model query is answerable only when its same-event reflective evidence links the exact RuleSummary result set. Native arbitration selects the answer disposition and reply plan.

effects.name: answer
effects.description: answers a graph-supported exact self-model query
